This year was one of the best for gaming of all time, with so many influential, important, popular, and enjoyable titles gracing fans. There are so many incredible Mario video games, but it is hard to beat Super Mario Galaxy, which is the final cherry on top of the 2007 cake. It may be a different vibe than a lot of the FPS titles or action-packed games, but it is a platforming masterclass that perfected the genre. The imaginative spherical gravity changed the gameplay to add a fun gimmick to the already flawless puzzles, proving why 2007 is the undefeated king of video games.

Players control either a British SAS squad or the US Marines, and must set out on a dangerous mission where they need to stop a Middle Eastern dictator from setting off a global nuclear war.

2007 had some of the greatest FPS titles of all time, and Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare is just the start. It is the pinnacle of the FPS genre in terms of action, having a tightly paced campaign and snappy gunplay. But this remarkable game is more than just a cinematic shooter, because its influence can still be felt in the genre today. Indeed, the franchise never got better than this seminal title.

'Halo 3'

Image via Microsoft Game Studios

The Xbox 360 was the go-to console for FPS games, and like Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Halo 3 was a definitive entry on the console. The franchise is Microsoft's crowning gem, and it peaked with its third entry. The fight against the Covenant seems to never end, but Master Chief hopes this time will finally be the end of this war.

The first handful of Halo games were all magnificent, but Halo 3 perfected the series with its polished gameplay and engaging story. This third entry into the long-running series defined split-screen multiplayer, just as a decade of co-op gaming was at its height. Fans have fond memories of this game that perfected the multiplayer servers and format, showing why it was a must-play game in 2007.

2007 was one of the best years for gaming of all time, meaning the choice for Game of the Year was the hardest up to that point, but it came down to two games, and one of them is BioShock. When the protagonist crash-lands in the ocean, they find refuge in a lone lighthouse. However, when descending further into it, they discover a failed Utopia plagued with political strife and terrifying genetically spliced monstrosities.

This year was one of the best for gaming of all time, with so many influential, important, popular, and enjoyable titles gracing fans. However, while they were feasting, BioShock was the pièce de resistance for many. Its political critique of Randian objectivism was captivating, and it was made even better because of the atmospheric backdrop that boosted the narrative. Today, BioShock remains a foundational piece of modern sci-fi and the clear choice for the 2007 Game of the Year.

'Super Mario Galaxy'

Image via Nintendo

As mentioned, the Game of the Year award was split between BioShock and one other game, which is now revealed to be Super Mario Galaxy. After Bowser kidnaps Princess Peach and takes her out to space, Mario must team up with Rosalina to venture around the cosmos and hop between the planets in order to find and rescue her from the evil King Koopa.

There are so many incredible Mario video games, but it is hard to beat Super Mario Galaxy, which is the final cherry on top of the 2007 cake. It may be a different vibe than a lot of the FPS titles or action-packed games, but it is a platforming masterclass that perfected the genre. The imaginative spherical gravity changed the gameplay to add a fun gimmick to the already flawless puzzles, proving why 2007 is the undefeated king of video games.
